description:
From fz-kdt.141 (2026-09-02, at 949dfce65 + the permutation stress).

THE MEASUREMENT. FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP's whole 268-escape
baseline -- 7 fixtures, the table in .agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md --
is decided by ONE order: the construction-wrapper member order
(flow.first_class_edges, a BTreeSet<CallableSurface> walked in
interned-id order = the type interner's mint order = the agenda's).
Sweeping the corpus under FZ_STRESS_PERMUTE_DISPATCH:

  settled          268   (00183 16, 00230 16, 00418 4, 00419 16,
                          00420 106, enum_take_drop_split 106,
                          unused_range_binding 4)
  wrappers:1        68   (five fixtures to ZERO; both take_drop 106->34)
  wrappers:6        20   (both take_drop 106->10)
  arms:reverse     268   0 fixtures move
  arms:<any seed>  268   0 fixtures move

Two facts fall out.

(1) NONE of the escape population is callsite-arrival-decided. Every
one of the 268 lives on the construction-wrapper surface. The census
is therefore not a fact about the program at all -- it is a fact about
which member the interner happened to mint first.

(2) THE SETTLED ORDER IS THE WORST MEASURED. Every permutation tried
lowers the count and none raises it; five of the seven fixtures have a
legal order with zero escapes. stdout and exit are identical
everywhere, on interp, JIT and AOT -- so the escapes are latent, but
the compiler is currently choosing the most exposed of the orders
available to it, by accident.

WHY IT IS NOT A SEATING RULE'S JOB TODAY. The members a wrapper cannot
separate are the fz-kdt.132 pair shape: two surfaces whose tuple test
is blind at a list position (the Scope-A carve-out), so whichever comes
first takes every value and the escapes are the values whose surface
that member does not name. A seat cannot fix what the test cannot see;
what CAN be decided is which member is first, and nothing decides it
today.

DIRECTIONS (not costed): (a) fz-kdt.138 makes the position testable and
the question dissolves -- check whether it takes all 268 with it before
building anything here; (b) failing that, order the members so the
WIDEST surface is first (the escape count is then bounded by what no
member names, not by mint order) -- note this is the fz-kdt.129 seat
question one layer over, and the same covers-vs-precision analysis has
to be done for it rather than assumed; (c) at minimum, the mint order
must stop being the decider, because it is the agenda's.

INSTRUMENT: the sweep is the recipe in .agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md
(section 'The two free orders'). Sequence after fz-kdt.132 / fz-kdt.138.
title: The settled construction-wrapper member order is the worst of the legal orders for surface-membership escapes
